fields.features_heading: What the Sheet Settles Before Tasting Day
fields.features_subheading: A chili cook off sign up sheet records who is cooking what. The one Emergent builds also plans power for every pot and the judging.
fields.feature_1:
Categories with their own entry caps

Lets each cook pick red, green, white, or vegetarian, with a separate cap on every category. A category that fills drops off the list, and the next cook sees only the open ones.
fields.feature_2:
An outlet question for every slow cooker

Asks each cook whether the pot needs power. Requests are totaled against the outlets you list for the room, so a short count shows up days before setup instead of at the wall.
fields.feature_3:
What is in the pot, stated up front

Asks each cook to name the meat and to tick beans, dairy, or peanuts in the recipe. Tasters read it on the table card, and a guest who skips pork can pass a pot without asking.
fields.feature_4:
Judges and cooks on one sheet

Adds a judges section next to the cook entries. A judge whose email also appears on an entry is flagged on your dashboard, so you can swap judges before the first spoon goes in.
fields.feature_5:
Table numbers in the reminder email

Emails every cook the evening before with their table number and the setup time at the hall. You choose the send time and the wording when you describe the sheet, and edit both.
fields.feature_6:
Entries kept in a database you own

Saves every cook and judge to a database you own, not a clipboard by the hall door. On paid plans, export the full code of the sheet to your GitHub repository and host it anywhere.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Cook-Offs Ran Their Sign-Ups
fields.tab_content_1:
Cook 11 waits its turn after the first 10 entries

Strathmoy Software caps its office cook-off at 10 entries, one per table in the break room. Wendall Tollison signs up eleventh with a smoked brisket chili and lands first on the waitlist. Entry 4 drops two days out. Wendall gets an email that his spot is open.
fields.tab_content_2:
Outlets for 12 pots, requests from 14

Twelve outlets line the hall at Bramhurst Volunteer Fire Company, and 14 of the 19 entries for its fall fundraiser ask for one. Setup lead Joaquina Castellucci gets an email that 2 slow cookers have no outlet. She borrows two power strips from the engine bay a week before the cook-off.
fields.tab_content_3:
Judges cleared of entering any pot

Judges sign up beside the cooks for the Fairhaugh Methodist Church fall festival, and each judge's email is checked against the 16 entries. Ardelle Quimby signed up to judge and also entered her green chili. Organizer Eustace Harcastle sees the flag, moves Ardelle to the cooks, and the other 4 judges are cleared.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each of 18 pots gets its own tasting card

Every pot at the Keswold Elementary PTA cook-off gets a number at sign-up, and 18 cooks entered this year. Each entry becomes a tasting card with the chili name, the meat, and anything else in the pot. Card 7 reads white chicken chili, chicken, contains dairy. PTA chair Rhett Yarborough prints all 18 the night before.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Chili Cook-Off Sign-Up Sheet
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a chili cook off sign up sheet that fits your tables and outlets, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick categories and cap each one
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask what a taster needs to know
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tell cooks how to arrive hot
fields.howto_step_1_des: Count the tables and the outlets you can reach without running cords across a walkway. The smaller number is your entry cap. A room with 8 outlets and 10 tables takes 8 slow cookers, plus any chili that arrives in an insulated pot.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose the categories your crowd cooks, such as traditional red and vegetarian, and give each its own cap. A category with only two entries makes a thin contest. Merge it into another before the sheet goes out, not on the day itself.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the chili name the way the cook wants it read aloud, then the meat and anything a taster might avoid. Leave the full recipe off the sheet. The tasting card needs only the ingredients, and each recipe stays with its cook.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Clemson Extension's slow cooker guidance says to heat food to steaming, 165 degrees F or above, before placing it into a preheated slow cooker at 140 degrees F or above. Put that line in the confirmation for cooks who make their chili the night before.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt with the entry cap, each category and its cap, the outlet question, and who hears when outlets run short. Emergent builds the sheet and the database behind it. Ask for edits in the same plain words later, such as a fifth category.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Collect only a name and an email from each judge. Plan for about three judges per 12 entries so nobody tastes past their limit. Ask the sheet to flag any judge who also entered, and swap that person before the scorecards go out.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Enter two test chilis yourself, one that asks for an outlet and one that fills a category. Check that the category closes, the outlet total moves, and the reminder email carries a table number. Delete both rows before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is a chili cook off sign up sheet?
faq_plan.ref: chili cook off sign up sheet
faq_plan.a: A chili cook off sign up sheet is the entry list for a chili contest: each cook's name, the chili they will bring, and its category. An online one also caps entries and records what each pot needs on the day, such as an outlet.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a chili cook off sign up sheet?
faq_plan.ref: chili cook off sign up sheet
faq_plan.a: Set the entry cap from the tables and outlets you have, then decide what each cook must tell you. Describe the sheet to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the form and the reminder emails. Share the link in the event invite.

faq_plan.q: What should a chili cook off sign up sheet template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with the cook's name and email, then the chili name and its category. Add the meat, a box for beans or dairy, and whether the pot needs an outlet. Put the date and setup time at the top, with any entry fee.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up a chili cook off sign up sheet for a work event?
faq_plan.a: Cap entries at one per table in the room you book, and set the deadline two days before a long lunch. Pick judges who did not enter, and post the winners the same afternoon. If the cook-off is one of several team events, add it to the learning and development survey questions HR sends after each one.

faq_plan.q: How many entries should a chili cook off sign up sheet allow?
faq_plan.a: Cap it at what your judges can taste and your outlets can power. Keep each judge's tasting list to 15 pots or fewer. For a bigger field, split the entries by category and give each category its own judges.

faq_plan.q: What categories should a chili cook off sign up sheet offer?
faq_plan.a: Pick from red, green, white, and vegetarian, and add a hot category if your crowd likes heat. Keep a category only if at least three cooks enter it. A people's choice award, voted on by every guest, can run alongside the judged categories.

faq_plan.q: What should I send people after they fill out a chili cook off sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Send each cook a confirmation of their entry and category right away. The morning after, send guests a short survey on which chili they would eat again and what to change. For wording, start from these audience survey questions. A survey Emergent builds saves every answer in a database you own, next to the sign-ups.

faq_plan.q: What reheating instructions belong on a chili cook off sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Tell cooks to reheat their chili on the stove, not in the slow cooker. Clemson Extension says reheating leftovers in a slow cooker is not recommended. Chili made the night before goes back on the stove until it steams, then into a slow cooker that is already hot.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a chili cook off sign up sheet online for free?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing the sheet, with no response caps on how many cooks sign up. Share the link by email or in a group text, and every entry lands in the same list.

faq_plan.q: How do I pick winners from a chili cook off sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Judges score numbers, not names, when every entry gets a number at sign-up. Judges rate each pot on taste and texture, and guests can cast a separate ballot for a people's choice award. For a lighter round between tastings, a few game survey questions keep the crowd busy while scores are counted.

plan.angle: The top 10 for chili cook off sign up sheet is printable grids from Etsy, Pinterest and template sites: blank lines for a cook's name and chili name. This page shows the sheet as a working entry system for the four events that run cook-offs: an office cook-off that caps at 10 entries and keeps a waitlist, a fire company fundraiser that checks outlet needs against the hall, a church fall festival whose judges sign up on the same sheet, and a PTA cook-off that turns each entry into a numbered tasting card. The how-to and FAQ add what printables skip: entry caps from tables and outlets, categories, what each pot contains, and getting chili to the table hot.
